memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown to the ground before the ark of the Lord, remaining there till evening. The elders of Israel did the same, and sprinkled dust on their heads. And Joshua said, "Alas, Sovereign Lord, why did you ever bring this people across the Jordan to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan! Pardon your servant, Lord. What can I say, now that Israel has been routed by its enemies?" — Josh 7:6-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua is devastated. He tears his clothes, falls facedown before the ark, and cries out to God all afternoon. His prayer is raw and honest, even accusing: "Why did you ever bring this people across the Jordan?" It almost echoes the grumbling of the wilderness generation — "if only we had stayed on the other side."

There is something comforting in seeing a great leader so shaken and confused. Joshua does not have it all together. He does not understand what has happened. And in his distress, he does the right thing: he takes his confusion straight to God. His theology in the moment is a bit off — he assumes God has failed them, when in fact sin in the camp is the problem. But at least he brings his honest heart before the Lord rather than turning away.

This teaches us how to handle our own dark, confused moments. When defeat comes and we cannot understand why, we can pour out our raw feelings to God. He is not offended by honest lament. The Psalms are full of such cries. God would rather we come to Him confused than not come at all.

Yet notice: Joshua asked "why" but had not yet asked "is there something wrong among us?" Sometimes our confusion in hard times is answered not by an explanation from God, but by a call to examine ourselves. When we bring our laments to God, we can also ask Him to search us (Ps 139:23-24). And we do so through Christ, our great High Priest, who invites us to come with confidence to find grace in our time of need (Heb 4:16).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When defeat or confusion comes, do you bring your honest feelings to God?
2. Is it possible that some confusion in your life is a call to self-examination?
3. How does having Christ as your High Priest encourage you to approach God honestly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, when I am confused and defeated, help me bring my honest heart to You. Search me, show me anything wrong, and meet me with Your grace. Amen.
